relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: A rotating military machine moves twenty-four thousand people into service each month.
Jashobeam commands the first month's division.
Perezite ancestry supports his place among commanders.
Dodai and Mikloth organize the second division.
Benaiah, a priest's son, commands the third.
Military reputation passes into leadership and then toward a son.
Asahel's place passes to Zebadiah after his death.
Shamhuth commands the fifth division.
Ira commands the sixth.
Helez commands the seventh.
Sibbecai commands the eighth.
Abiezer commands the ninth.
Maharai commands the tenth.
Benaiah commands the eleventh.
Heldai commands the twelfth.
Tribal administration begins with Reuben and Simeon.
Levi and Aaron receive leaders.
Judah and Issachar receive leaders.
Zebulun and Naphtali receive leaders.
Ephraim and half-Manasseh receive leaders.
Gileadite Manasseh and Benjamin receive leaders.
Dan closes the tribal roster.
Those twenty and younger are left outside David's count.
Joab's unfinished census remains under the shadow of collective catastrophe.
Royal wealth is distributed across treasuries and regional storehouses.
Ezri oversees the people who work the soil.
Shimei and Zabdi oversee vineyards and wine.
Baal-hanan and Joash oversee trees and oil.
Shitrai and Shaphat oversee cattle in two regions.
Obil the Ishmaelite cares for camels; Jehdeiah cares for donkeys.
Jaziz the Hagarite cares for flocks within David's vast estate.
Family and education shape access to royal counsel.
Ahithophel and Hushai stand beside the king with futures the list does not tell.
Counsel and army command remain concentrated in a small network.

contemplative_note: The kingdom's visible strength is twelve armies. Its actual life is fields, vines, olives, wine, oil, herds, camels, donkeys, flocks, and the people caring for them. A spiritual reading shifts attention from those who command royal power to those whose labor and living creatures make it possible.
